notes.title: Thank you for supporting our game!
notes.content:
Dear players,
 
Thank you for supporting our game! We are grateful for the 98% positive rating on Steam, which exceeded our expectations. We acknowledge that our first project, "A Guidebook of Babel," has some shortcomings. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to improve the game's imperfections.

In the week since the game's launch, we have been continuously working on optimizations. We have addressed issues that were prominently highlighted, such as progression-blocking situations, save-game problems, and control-related concerns. Next, we will focus on dealing with text display issues on small screens, etc. Moving forward, we are committed to constant improvement to offer all of you a better gaming experience.

We appreciate your feedback. You can connect with us on various platforms, including Steam, Twitter, and Discord. If you have any feedback, you can let us know via the link below：

Your comments are highly valued, and we are eager to hear from you!

Best regards,

notes.title: FQA before release
notes.content:
1、About our team
We are StarryStarry, an indie game studio. A Guidebook Of Babel is our first title.

2、When will the game be unlocked on Steam?
The game will be unlocked on August 2, 2023 7:00 PM PDT.

3、About the price
The game is priced at 12.7 USD after the first-week discount.

4、Does your game support experience on Steam Deck?
You can play normally on Steam Deck.

5、Does your game support experience on Mac OS?
You can enjoy the game on your Mac.

6、Does the game support cloud save？
Yes.

7、The required space of the game is only 300MB. How long can we play this game?
8-10 hours.

8、Does the game have multiple endings and branches?
No, the game has only one ending.The player seems to be playing a detective who is searching for the road to this ending in the fog.

9、What is the inspiration for game production?
A small incident from the past led me to imagine this bizarre world after death. I hope this world can provide you with a different perspective to think about life and regret.

10、In addition to the standard edition of the game, will there be DLC or deluxe edition?
There will be a deluxe edition, which includes the game itself, the original soundtrack and the digital artbook collection. Buying the deluxe edition will be more cost-effective than buying the above three separately.

notes.title: A Guidebook of Babel Closed Beta Test!
notes.content:
Hello, passengers. We're ecstatic to announce that the Closed Beta Test for A Guidebook of Babel will take place from 5 November to 11 November. Please see the details below:

[b]About our Game:[/b]
Rewrite the past and change the future! A Guidebook of Babel is a plot-driven adventure game with the unique "Butterfly Effect" mechanic.

Experience a fantastical afterlife journey, ride through monsoons in the belly of a puffer fish, and board a giant ship called Babel where the wishes and regrets of our travelers are intertwined.

[b]Purpose of the Closed Beta Test:[/b]
We want to know your play experience, identify any potential issues, and address them to make our game even better.
A feedback survey will be sent out to everyone who participates in the closed beta test, and the results will be shared directly with the development team. Depending on your feedback, we may invite you to an in-depth 1-on-1 follow-up interview.

[b]Participation Requirements:[/b]
- Must be at least 18 years old.
- Will need to sign an NDA
- Must test the game thoroughly and provide feedback via the survey

[b]Application Period and Selection Announcement:[/b]
Complete this [url=https://forms.gle/3vZteecUoUjwFM2z7]questionnaire[/url] by November 2 to submit your application. We will select the participants according to the information you fill in, and the results will be announced on November 4.

[b]Test time:[/b]
November 5-November 11

[b]Bonus:[/b]
- Everyone selected for the closed beta test will be added to the game's "Thank You" list
- Participants will be gifted with the official version of the game + OST + Artbook

notes.title: Enter the Dragon | Kickstarter News
notes.content:
Hey everyone, Gardener here again.

I'd love to open with some friendly banter - but there's no time, dammit! I've got some big news to share, so buckle up...

Okay, where to start....... Dragons! Yes, always start with dragons...

We're taking part in [b]Enter the Dragon[/b], the steam event which officially got underway today (April 22 - 29). Enter the Dragon is a celebration of unique and interesting games from the Greater China region...and as developers based in Shanghai, that includes us!

As part of the event, we'll have the following:
[olist]
[*] A demo of the game will be available during the event, and can be downloaded from our store page. The demo features two stages from the final game, so jump in and let us know what you think!
[/olist]
[olist]
[*] We'll be hosting a gameplay livestream on [b]April 24 at 21:00(EDT)[/b] over on the [b]EtD page[/b] here: https://store.steampowered.com/sale/enterthedragon  Please come join us!
[/olist]

But wait, there's more!

A Guidebook of Babel is coming to [b]Kickstarter[/b]! When? [b]May 10[/b], to be precise. Our page will be going live soon at this address: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/pixmain/a-guidebook-of-babel-an-afterlife-adventure-0

Our goal is to create the best experience possible for players of our game, and after careful consideration we have decided that utlizing Kickstater will enable us to get across the development finish line and deliver the experience we envisaged from the very beginning.

We'll have more to share real soon, but that's all for today's update! As always, we welcome feedback regarding our newly released trailer - and don't forget to say "hi" during the upcoming livestream. 

Gardener out.

notes.title: Babel devblog - March
notes.content:
Come in...this is Gardener! Can you hear me?
Okay, I should be coming through loud and clear now. It's that time of year again - Spring is making its presense known across the Earth's northern hemisphere, and I guess many of you have already said goodbye to your winter jackets. The Babel was been particularly busy this Spring. Allow me to elaborate. Let's start with our two new team members: Taro and Kaino!

Meow-ow-ow...meow-ooh! 
An ailurophile who likes to paint using kitty paws, Taro is a highly skilled artist who was discovered drifting through space, or maybe she just escaped from a backyard.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/3def3dae9f32b393988435bf69ec02115e0ef411.png[/img]
Kaino, meanwhile, is a senior mechanical engineer hailing from an unknown galaxy, and has been put to work constructing the game's internal systems. Cursed with considerable creative pride, his Kung-fu skills, even more than the "heavy machinery" he carries, have left his peers totally flabbergasted.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/ec9e4edad39a500723a3ed9f7524274be4ec156a.png[/img]

Next, we've made some huge strides in terms of optimizing the originial note system.  How significant are the changes? Let's just say...we almost completely remade this part of the game!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/098aa8967e1688d09566d77b626cfe942d10180b.png[/img]
We hope that these logical new designs allow for a more intuitive reasoning experience, while also providing greater visual feedback. As we have highlighted before, our goal is not to create an overly difficult game designed to 'torture' players. Instead, we want to combine puzzles and narrative to surprise and engage them. The aforementioned optimizations have validated our design philosophy in this regard.

The third item on the agenda is something entirely new for our game. Just take a look at this picture:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/3c6f32f900f165defc7161661e99d6a4e592d5b9.png[/img]
Can you guess what it is? The answer is......it's an all-new rewriting challenge! To put it simply, if you want to rewrite something, you must first pass a fun mini game! Here, players will need to adjust something inside the object so that it ends up in the desired state. However, you must first be absolutely sure of the state you want, as this will end up triggering the butterfly effect!
Finally, one last thing before I hang up the communicator...

In addition to everything mentioned above, we're also paying special attention to the fine details of each performance on the stage. After all, I've long harbored dreams of producing movies, so this type of expert direction and performance micromanagement comes naturally to me!

That's it for today's dispatch. Thanks for listening, and I wish you all clear skies and calm seas ahead. Gardener out.
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/89cb77f01e7c87c2c389bbe626b34f50584f0096.png[/img]

notes.title: Babel devblog - December
notes.content:
Hi, this is Gardener!

Again, the end of the year is coming soon…In other words, are you guys on Earth getting ready to welcome a new year? Have you picked up the energy and left some unforgettable memories in the past year? Well…please cherish these memories no matter they are good or bad because I am always looking forward to your stories when you get on the Babel in our game~

Back to the game, the best word for describing our game for the past year is… set-sail? But the Babel, this little tattered ship had been sailing in no man’s sky for nearly 3 years, and we had absorbed cosmic rays enough for over three years as well. Ahh, every cloud has a silver lining, which is more accurate for our situation for the past year. At our most desperate, the ship's radar keenly caught an asteroid where we hurriedly landed to resupply. We poured fuel into the engine and repaired the damaged shell. Also, we recruited a new crew. When the engines fired up, I seemed to be watching my space shuttle rising up... We made it(ㄒoㄒ)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/b15b2c7eb9edd3fb3668cd49e8c7f40f88bc051a.png[/img]
[i]Discussing new game features...[/i]

After restarting our journey, we accelerated our work efficiency for rapidly improving the completion of A Guidebook of Babel with our new crews. During the journey, we also experienced the period of gelling with team members and the time of self-examination. Luckily, these obstacles quickly became a steppingstone to our next stop. We made it together. Now the next stop is the completion of A Guidebook of Babel!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/2610147921be6bf99223b8369a0234de47a9036c.jpg[/img]
[i]Guess it! It would come up in our full version![/i]

Yet a lot of interesting things have indeed happened in the past year. They are not all pleasant, however, I still like to write it down! What I like the most is the designing the game themed gift although it took a lot of time. Of course, I never planned to escape the task of writing the scripts! Although anyone with a discerning eye can see, I did burn out my brain several times by accident while writing the scripts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/25314cd10724707b5e0aeb3e03148638ad3dfc76.png[/img]
[i] The draft pf mystery toy boxes. Ps: it’s a pity that the 2X2 set design for the boxes were denied.[/i]

The most exhausting ‘business’ is to attend events. We need to arrive at the booth very early, standing there for the whole day. Then introduce the game to every gamer who wants to try it till we got thirsty and tired. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/20396e6e28998d012822fe44ec7f9c6882c65a44.png[/img]
[i]When I exhausted, I really want to swallow a questionnaire to make it disappear![/i]

Seriously, the most nervous thing for me is the chat show recording. This is the first time in my life that I participated in such a big show recording! Hmmm… in fact I have participated a show recording in HongKong before when I was still a college student. This time I had ‘Babel’ with me...and unexpectedly became one of the protagonists?! Yoh, the spotlight I’m coming although I forgot my words. If only I had the communication skills of the Chef Lanqi.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/2d415d860179981aa089e85b0e8762196809fa14.png[/img]
[i]What? Just Bronze Three Winner? Never mind, Dripwood awards (an award in Babel game) by the Chef is the highest![/i]

The most difficult moment... may be the role switch. Work is only part of life after all. The challenges that life brings to me are much more tough than the difficulties of game development. For me, Gardener, a game developer of the Babel game, and a husband and father, are both the roles that I need to switch again and again. On either side, never being absent is the hardest thing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/adcebfaa7a1e99ad9f9d7d765ad00b3fe42af060.png[/img]
[i]Holding my daughter's hand in the hospital.
[/i]

Well, how did you guys spend your year? In the new year, do you plan to stop or continue to move forward? Anyway, don't forget you have Gardener’s reporting with you although sometimes it will not be updated very frequently lol. I will be always here for you and happy new year! The destination planet of this voyage is already very close.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/208e046300bac6baf51252b1c9c242472e392606.png[/img]

So that's all for today, see you soon, folks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/adcebfaa7a1e99ad9f9d7d765ad00b3fe42af060.png[/img]

notes.title: Babel Digest Monthly | October 2021
notes.content:
Hi everyone! Gardener reporting in again! I propose we discuss a new topic today...of course it's connected to Babel's plot and puzzles -- "Managing relationships in the age of Time Travel". Yep! You heard right.

Don't turn away just yet based on how academically off-putting this sounds...what we're about to discuss is in fact quite plebeian...

Alright, so you all know "Re:Zero - Starting Life in Another World"? First season in, the protagonist Subaru goes through tremendous challenges with the other characters as he travels through time, but at last, he builds a long-lasting bond with them. I couldn't help but wonder...Do these kinds of relationships really exist?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/45c5829af56cdaae2b90b3f9d4f4d3d36c3f51d4.jpg[/img]
[i]Re:Zero - Starting Life in Another World
[/i]
Subaru sure did keep all memories from the past...for the others, not so much, as they only have the freshest memory from their time. In other words, whatever happened in alternate universes wouldn't matter to them. Perhaps...Subaru's just a "newcomer" in their eyes. Who is this newcomer to these people? There is probably some interaction but nothing close to a long-lasting bond...

Sorta counter-intuitive...isn't it? What's really happened is...we're experiencing a few flashes of what happened in the show in our minds. And when we reminisce on the various dynamics between the characters, we can't help but be reminded of the critical moments. Thus, a sense of "profound" connection is formed. Voila! Yep...even though those things never happened.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/d38e45d9878a0e8e69064f0a1611a3610edd10b9.jpg[/img]
[i]"The newcomer" Subaru
[/i]
It's as if we're blindfolded to have a greater sense of enjoyment for the story! I guess this is why we have a "cracked image" of history. Am I right? Well, for Subaru, people will probably see him as the most "familiar" stranger. 

[i][b]So how is all this related to Babel?[/b][/i]

Well... isn't it clear? The keyword on Babel is "rewrite history", naturally, we'll encounter many questions related to time travel. For everyone on Babel, their "latest" memory stays with the most recent occurrence --- see the connection there? But in the eyes of the player...through rounds of rewinding and occurrences, the details become blurry, allowing us to reminisce on our interactions with the characters when we meet them "again". 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/1253e467d405c1bf0981f01c723b8e8f0f15bf87.jpg[/img]
[i]The timeline recorded in the game as the story develops, but only as "updated" as what has played out already
[/i]

In an earlier episode on Babel, one can gift this little girl a stick of cotton candy. As one proceeds unto other tasks and the story continues, this occurrence is buried and turns into something that has never happened before. When you traverse across time to come back to the very same point and see that the little girl already has the stick of cotton candy in her hands, which someone else gifted...while it is the first time you are meeting her...yet it feels as if you've known each other for a long time.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/bc29b234db93be6cf38cdb9e164d81507701525e.png[/img]
[i]Head chef generously hands out candy, Lake swallows within three
[/i]

This is a technique used widely on Babel...guaranteed to bedazzle you.
The same reason why people call screenwriters the magicians on paper! You have much to look forward to! *looking pleased*

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/cc91dac0966cd62abac08fa95f1c1965c6befac4.jpg[/img]
[i]Magic powers don't come easy, why not use it more?
[/i]

So that's all for today, folks! Did you get all that?
Hard to believe I've gone on for so long on this theory...I guess I could find employment in teaching if all goes south! Fingers crossed that won't happen... we've got a long way to go for Babel! Catch you all later!

You can follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/GoBabelgame]Twitter[/url] or chat with us on [url=https://discord.gg/qSXS7EDqVd]Discord[/url]!

notes.title: Babel Devblog – August
notes.content:
[i]Bzz —— Bzz ——[/i]
This is Gardener speaking! July has come and gone, and the heat here was a killer. Speaking of weather, care for a forecast? We plan on holding a round of tests once our current task is completed in order to check the tutorial's design. We encourage you to sign up once the time has come!

On another topic, allow me to discuss the genesis of the butterfly effect in the game. We draw our inspiration from a movie called The Butterfly Effect and a manga and anime called Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World. We learnt a great deal in terms of narration from the former, and the latter taught us how to introduce and develop relationships between protagonists and other characters. But let's just talk about the movie for now. I'll talk about Re:Zero's Subaru in the next development log.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/f46a54471e2d7dc6f591de73b7fca1b276699de7.jpg[/img]

For the newcomers around here, I'll quickly introduce the gameplay of the game. A Guidebook of Babel follows four characters, and players play as the character of each separate storyline. Those storylines are further divided into scenes, arranged in chronological order, and each scene focuses on a specific subject. In each scene, players have a quest to accomplish and, in order to do that, they have to trigger the Butterfly Effect in specific places to go back in time and change the future!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/c8d7253b48d65a8f2c26a1241e55f609ba4b5b57.jpg[/img]

You should have an idea of what the game is like now, so… Have you watched The Butterfly Effect? The plot is very simple: One day, the protagonist wakes up with the ability to go back in time (to oversimplify it), so he starts to go back in time to modify tragic events in his past that affected him or his loved ones, over and over again.
So, what did we take away from this movie? Obviously, it's the protagonist's superpower! But done differently, through what we call: Rewriting. In each scene, it is possible to enter Rewriting mode at any time and rewrite an item or character in the scene. However, only specific items or characters can be rewritten, thus revealing hidden interactions and possibilities. And selecting said interactions will then trigger the butterfly effect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/f02e5d84a3850726ab917739d0abba8de6374977.jpg[/img]

I think everyone is now very familiar with the "search and find" aspect of the game. Players have to find that one special interaction inside a complex, almost overwhelming, story. But in order to find that specific interaction, players don't have to go in blind! The trick is to first understand what sort of trouble the protagonist is in, what is preventing him or her from completing his/her quest. Then, they need to think about the cause of the trouble and associate it with the scene's plot to find the special item/character at the root of the problem.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/0baf268b82b2f7c3f71a45d73a9c489b05f536b8.png[/img]

Of course, it is difficult to find the root cause of the problem without some tools to help. Fortunately, those tools have been part of the game for some time already: event signs and notes! When exploring a scene, players will see a series of event signs, that will help them understand the chain of events that lead to this particular problem. In the notebook, a mysterious voice will ask questions related to the quest at hand. If players filled in the event signs correctly, they can answer the questions without any issue. The whole question and answer process is to help create the chain of events in players' mind, so that they can find the solution.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/af44ef48f5af390b83a9abffea6170cdaf0f0295.png[/img]

Once players find the special item/character and interact with it, this seemingly insignificant change will trigger the "plot tsunami". Whether the "new" scenario is more surprising and exciting, it all depends on the imagination of our wordsmith and mine though!
So, that is what we learnt from The Butterfly Effect movie. What do you think? Interesting, eh? Are you ready to challenge yourself? Don't forget to follow us so as not to miss any upcoming news, especially the news about the test rounds! We count on you to sign up when it's live!

[i]Gardener, out! Bzz—[/i]

notes.title: A Guidebook of Babel's Steam Next Fest Q&A
notes.content:
[i]We wish to thank all the players who shared their feedback about the exclusive demo of A Guidebook of Babel that we put online for Steam Next Fest.
Before the event is officially over, we have selected the most recurring questions to give you what we hope are satisfying answers. If, after reading this Q&A, you still have questions, please contact us either on the Steam page directly or on [url=https://twitter.com/GoBabelgame]Twitter[/url] or [url=https://discord.gg/MERx8VzG9B]Discord[/url]. We'll promise to give you an answer as fast as possible![/i]


[olist]
[*] Will the puzzles of the final version of the game be more challenging than the demo's?
Of course! After playing the exclusive demo, players should have used the butterfly effect twice to solve puzzles, which only require one rewrite to do so. In the final game, we will experiment more about the unpredictable outcomes that result from using the butterfly effect, and [b]players may have to rewrite several elements in order to unlock their path[/b].

[*] How many main characters are there in the game?
[b]The final game will tell the stories of the four main characters of the game[/b], whereas the demo allows to play two of them. The third main character can be seen at the very end of the demo, and you will have to play the game to understand what relationship he has with the others! As for the fourth main characters, it is still somewhat of a secret, but we will introduce more about them in the coming months, so stay tuned!

[*] When will the game be released? Will it release as a complete title or will it come out in "episodes"?
PC version of the game will be released [b]either at the end of this year or at the beginning of the next one[/b], depending on the completion rate of the plot at the time. 
Mobile versions (Android and iOS) are scheduled for release during Q2 2022. We will post announcements once we know more about that. 

[*] After the end of Steam Next Fest, will the demo still be available on some other platforms?
Our China-based players can meet us during this year's edition of [b]BiliBili World[/b] in Shanghai, from July 7 to 11.
We are contemplating [b]opening a kickstarter this Autumn[/b] (if you like the game, please help support it), for which the demo will serve as a showcase. And we are also [b]toying with the idea of getting testers for a closed beta[/b] who would help us improve the flow of the game and find any weird bug (we have found one already, we expect it's not the only one). You are all cordially invited to [b]follow us on our different social media[/b], such as [url=https://twitter.com/GoBabelgame][b]Twitter[/b][/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/GoBabelgame][b]Facebook[/b][/url], [url=https://discord.gg/MERx8VzG9B][b]Discord[/b][/url], etc. in order to stay up-to-date with the latest news!

[*] The game does not feel like it is finalized, for instance the tutorial is not polished, there is no menu, no way to quit the game, it is not optimized, etc. Will you fix those issues in the future?
[b]The tutorial is a work in progress and we're exploring different ways to enhance the onboarding process of players[/b] and make everything more user-friendly.
And don't worry, we will add an exit button and a "real" menu in the future. As mentioned, the demo is a work in progress, and we have much work to do!
[b]Performances of the game are already undergoing optimization[/b], but we won't stop here. Our goal is to make our game available to most, so we will keep optimizing the game so that it runs flawlessly on as many systems as possible.

[*] After launching the game, I experienced some slow-down of the game, has it been fixed?
In the first two days of the Steam Next Fest, several players have reported witnessing an extreme slow-down of the game upon launching the introduction cutscene. After a little investigation, we have been able to determine that the issue affected players whose system settings were set to specific regions (mainly France, Italy, Germany, Spain, etc.), but we have been able to fix this issue and you are now able to play the game as intended! If you haven't tried it before, please launch the game on Steam again to update the build!
[/olist]

Lastly, please note that Steam Next Fest will be offline in 36 hours, so there is not much time left for you to play the demo if you haven't tried it already!

notes.title: Babel Devblog - May
notes.content:
Bzz—

This is Gardener speaking. From today on, we promise to communicate at the previously agreed-upon time, as per the Babel’s strict regulations. Should we fail to uphold this most solemn promise, then… Forget we ever made it in the first place! Are we not allowed a little leniency in our communication schedule?

Well, back to the matter at hand. Where did we stop last time? Ah, right, we mentioned the merry lot who partied a little too merrily on the deck and got themselves inebriated, flouting the strict regulations prohibiting the consumption of alcohol above deck by crewmates. Believe me though, once Javert is done with whatever errand he has to run, he is going to remind them who is in charge… Wait a minute, did he not already catch one?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/f3f8ca4739f83524d2b0570135b53895e2d7bbc7.jpg[/img]
[i]We cannot speak of this, lest we reveal too much[/i]

We have also reached a new stage in the development of the game, shifting the our focus from the boat to Dripwood Forest. The last of our four main characters will start her adventure within those woods. This lovely lady, who will remain anonymous for the time being — after all, a lady must maintain the mystery — is one hell of a pilot. Furthermore, her unique skills and abilities allow her to remain stunningly beautiful under any circumstances! How awesome is that?

In a very unsurprising twist, our lady pilot is suddenly and most unexpectedly faced with difficulties. Aaw naaw! Her engine is coughing up smoke, and we can all agree that this is rarely conducive to an enjoyable flight. What? You cannot see the smoke? … Well, um, we did not have time to add it to the visuals, so just pretend like it’s there. Cough, cough, the smoke is irritating my respiratory tract. Cough, cough See? It is easy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/643321086fbf2faa95e71de767630a47e545e88c.jpg[/img]
[i]This is not an ideal place to be stranded on[/i]

To follow up on the stage of development, we have started porting to Nintendo Switch. Many thanks to Rick, whose efforts really paved the way for this. In the hopefully not-so-distant future, everyone will be able to carry a piece of Babel on them. At all times. And for all Eternity. Neat!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39170071/068e11fbfb483eb49b4fef1e834bd0bb2788cb36.png[/img]
[i]Our expectations are high, what about yours?[/i]

I think that wraps it up for this communication. This was Gardener, signing off.
[i]Do you think they’ll notice we didn’t speak much of the alliance? I’m afraid they’ll think we’re just going through the motions without… Oops, the mic is still on![/i]

Bzzz—

Hello! This is [b]Gardener[/b] again! * speaking proudly * The inspiration behind the adventures on the Babel first came from me...I single-handedly am responsible for the most important world view of the game and its plotlines. * coughs * Of course, the art style has definitively made us stand out. notes.title: That one drunken night...on the Babel
